solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: No piano in Sex Pistols' music and one new chord — or is that harsh?

indicators.note: No in front of piano says that letter is dropped from the music word

parts.note: the Sex Pistols were the classic punk band
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
the Roman numeral for one is I
a chord can be named by its root note, here D

explanation.surface: A music critic asks whether stripping the piano from punk and adding a lone chord is a cruel thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh treatment is cruel or lacking in sympathy, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Inauspicious start to detente following peacekeepers opposing what Christian soldiers march as

indicators.note: following says the first letter of detente comes after the other pieces

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces
the hymn Onward, Christian Soldiers continues 'marching as to war'

indicators.note: start to picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A poor beginning to peace talks follows UN troops resisting crusading marchers.
explanation.walkthrough: The hymn line 'Onward, Christian soldiers, marching as to war' supplies the middle letters; 'opposing' is only link padding in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means unfortunate or unfavourable, close in sense to ill-omened.

clue.text: Potentially heavy toll with Left going for European — prepare to pray

indicators.note: going for means one letter is swapped out in favour of another

parts.note: a knell is the slow, solemn toll of a bell, often heavy with grief

explanation.surface: A death bell rings out and someone European steps in to lead the prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down on one's knees is the posture people adopt before praying.

clue.text: Plainclothes officers infiltrating fanatics whose cover is non-existent?

indicators.note: infiltrating means the officers get inside the group of fanatics

parts.note: nuts are enthusiasts or fanatics, as in fitness nuts
DIs, detective inspectors, are police officers who work out of uniform

explanation.surface: Undercover police get inside an extremist group, whose cover is blown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests an undercover identity; here it means clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists wear no clothes, so their covering is absent.

clue.text: Wore drape jacket extremely tight?

parts.note: wore is read loosely as was, as in was a certain type of person by dress
the long drape jacket was the uniform of the Ted, or Teddy boy

explanation.surface: Someone in a long, close-fitting drape coat looks squeezed into it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first two words as 'was a Ted': Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style drape jackets. 'Tight' is then not snug clothing but drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for drunk, and being very drunk is being smashed or wrecked, a slang synonym.

clue.text: No-hoper was a candidate too

parts.note: too means also, in addition
to run in an election is to stand as a candidate

explanation.surface: A hopeless contender also stood in the election.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser or also-starter who never had a chance is a hopeless contender.

clue.text: Art nouveau popular after Klee's impenetrable canvas

indicators.note: after places the word for popular behind the painter's first name
nouveau, new, signals the letters are made over in a fresh order

parts.note: Paul Klee was the Swiss-German painter
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Art Nouveau proves popular after Klee's work on an impenetrable canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art nouveau' looks like the style but the second word signals a remix of ART.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a heavy waterproof sheet of canvas that nothing gets through.

clue.text: Unfinished soft cheese among some French leftovers

indicators.note: among says the cheese goes in the middle of the French word

parts.note: des is the French for some

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter of the cheese is removed

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: Half-eaten soft cheese among French leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered rubble or remains, a synonym for leftovers.

clue.text: Manage visit as well having dropped round

parts.note: to attend a place is to visit or go to it

indicators.note: having dropped tells us one letter has fallen out of the word for as well

parts.note: as well means too, also
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone manages to pay a call and drops in as well.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal with or look after something is to handle it, a phrasal-verb synonym of manage.

clue.text: Abroad Germany and Italy's position is better by far

parts.note: out means abroad, away from home
D is the international car code for Germany
I is the international car code for Italy
a stance is a position or attitude

explanation.surface: Away from home, Germany and Italy's standing is much better.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave rivals far behind in a race is to beat them by a long way.

clue.text: Butcher or Best becoming flash on and off

indicators.note: to butcher something is to mangle it, so these letters are hacked into a new order

explanation.surface: Two footballers named Butcher and Best, one apparently turning into a show-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Terry Butcher and George Best were famous footballers, which disguises 'Butcher' as a name rather than the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroboscopic lamp is a light that blinks rapidly, as in a nightclub, so the noun names this kind of flashing light.

clue.text: Missing nothing in what can be boring

indicators.note: in says the letter for nothing goes inside the boring tool

parts.note: an awl is a pointed tool used for boring holes
nothing, zero, is the letter O

explanation.surface: Nothing is missing from something that may be dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' suggests tedious, but it means making holes, which is what an awl does.
explanation.definitionFit: The military acronym for absent without leave describes a soldier who has gone missing.

clue.text: Drunken Australian orgy

indicators.note: drunken suggests reeling about, so the letters stagger into another order

explanation.surface: A wild party thrown by an inebriated Aussie.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman winter festival gave its name to any wild revelry or riotous celebration.

clue.text: Paid arranger perhaps to accept key change to create moving hymn

indicators.note: a key change is a shift from one musical key to another, here from F to C

parts.note: an arranger who is paid for the work is a pro, the opposite of an amateur

explanation.surface: A paid musician is asked to agree to a change of key to produce a stirring hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: F and C are both musical keys, so the 'key change' swaps one letter for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn sung while the choir and clergy walk in procession is one that is moving in the literal sense.

clue.text: Lunch counter and ace fare it served up

indicators.note: served up suggests food dished out, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lunch counter with excellent food that it dishes out.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service restaurant where diners queue at a counter is a typical lunch spot.

clue.text: Model railway coach ready to start

parts.note: to coach is to train someone
set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

explanation.surface: A model railway carriage is all set to begin its journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a railway carriage but is the verb meaning teach.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy railway with track and locomotives is sold as a boxed set.

clue.text: First vegetables in their field? These 9 5

parts.note: first, at the head, means at the front
runner beans are vegetables, and a field of them holds runners

explanation.surface: The earliest crop in a vegetable field, which leaves the others behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is OUTDISTANCE and 5 is ALSO-RAN: the leaders leave the also-rans behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaders in a race or contest outpace those who trail behind, the no-hopers.

clue.text: Coal bins without lid converted into containers for lubricants

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged
the lid of a word is its first letter, so bins loses its top

explanation.surface: Old coal bins with no lids are turned into oil holders.
explanation.definitionFit: Cans with spouts hold oil for lubricating machinery.

clue.text: University listen about item in canteen?

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters of listen are rearranged

explanation.surface: University students are told to pay attention to something in the dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: A canteen is also a box of cutlery, so 'in canteen' points to a knife or fork rather than a refectory.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen of cutlery holds knives, forks and spoons, each a piece of kitchen ware.

clue.text: Addled American celebrated by bards of Bow Bells

definitions.meaning: addled, as of an egg, means gone rotten and infected

definitions.text: American celebrated by bards of Bow Bells

explanation.surface: Confused American praised by Cockney poets.
explanation.walkthrough: A true Cockney is born within the sound of the bells of St Mary-le-Bow in London; Cockney rhyming slang shortens a rhyming phrase to its first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten eggs are infected or putrid, and rhyming slang calls an American a septic, a crossword-friendly slang sense.

clue.text: It'll be the death of me training mum to get to grips with tango

definitions.text: It'll be the death of me

parts.note: PE, physical education, is training at school

indicators.note: getting to grips with means holding something, so the silence word holds the letter for tango

parts.note: mum, as in keeping mum, means silence
tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone groans that a mother's training sessions involving the tango will kill them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother but means silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is a deadly epidemic, so it is the thing that will kill the speaker.

clue.text: Dismiss the odds of cheekier one being likely to succeed

indicators.note: dismissing the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones of the word cheekier

explanation.surface: Someone ignores the poor chances of a cheeky person succeeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds' looks like betting odds but means the first, third, fifth and seventh letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A successor in line to a title or estate is the person expected to succeed to it.

clue.text: Spooner's study doctor used for girls' night out

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of two words are exchanged

parts.note: a den is a private study or room
Doctor Who is the time-travelling BBC hero, often just called the Doctor

explanation.surface: Spooner's study is taken over by a doctor for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of DEN and WHO gives HEN DO; the W of WHO is silent, so the swap is by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen party, the bride-to-be's celebration with friends, is a classic night out for women.

clue.text: What should come with ribs — portion of Harvester nachos?

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Diners wonder whether nachos at Harvester, a British pub restaurant chain, belong with the spare ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: Breastbones, in the anatomical plural, are joined to the ribs in the chest.

clue.text: Sense is a misused facility

indicators.note: misused says the letters are put to the wrong use, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Good sense has been put to bad use as a talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Facility can mean ease or effortlessness in doing something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Loophole may be what let the cat out of the bag so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak says the word is heard, not seen

parts.words: what let the cat out of the bag
parts.note: a cat would scratch its way out of a bag with its claws

explanation.surface: A legal loophole was what gave the secret away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let the cat out of the bag' normally means revealing a secret; here it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is often a single term or provision in a contract, an example of the wider category.

clue.text: Charity shelters duck with temperature practically

indicators.note: shelters means the charity word holds the duck inside it

parts.note: alms are charitable gifts to the poor
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A charity gives a duck shelter and warmth, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero, so it gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Practically, meaning very nearly, is a synonym of nearly or all but.
